slides.title: How gravity was discovered
slides.caption: From a falling apple to a law that reaches the Moon: the same pull that drops an apple holds the Moon in its orbit, and Newton's inverse-square law generalises it to all masses.
slides.narration: The story of gravity's discovery runs as a chain. It starts with the falling apple — the everyday pull toward Earth. Newton's leap was to see the Moon as perpetually falling, kept in orbit by the same force. That force weakens with the square of distance, and the inverse-square law, checked against the Moon's motion, becomes universal gravitation — one law for the apple and the planets alike.

slides.title: The apple falls
slides.caption: Newton watches the apple fall from the tree — the everyday pull toward Earth that begins his chain.
slides.bridge: Start where the story does: the apple drops.

slides.title: The Moon falls around Earth
slides.caption: The Moon perpetually falls around Earth — the same pull that drops the apple, now seen in 3D as an orbit with the focus at Earth.
slides.bridge: The apple falls straight down — but the Moon falls sideways, forever missing the ground.
slides.narration: Here is the Moon's orbit in three dimensions — the second stage of the chain. Earth sits at the focus, and the Moon perpetually falls toward it, its sideways motion keeping it in orbit. The same pull that drops the apple holds the Moon in this path.

slides.title: Newton thinks
slides.caption: Newton, pondering the falling apple and the orbiting Moon — the leap that joins them into one law.
slides.bridge: And the man who joined them — Newton, thinking it through.
slides.narration: And here is Newton himself, pondering the falling apple and the orbiting Moon. The dashed curve behind him is the mathematics taking shape in his mind — the inverse-square law that unites the apple and the Moon into one universal pull.

slides.title: The inverse-square law
slides.caption: The leap made law: the pull weakens with the square of distance, and the inverse-square law generalises to all masses as universal gravitation.
slides.bridge: So the same pull that drops the apple and holds the Moon must weaken with distance —
slides.narration: Newton's leap becomes a law. The pull weakens with the square of the distance, and the inverse-square law, checked against the Moon's motion, generalises to all masses as universal gravitation.

from manim import *

class GeneratedScene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # ---- Title ----
        title = Text("Newton's Apple", font_size=44, color=WHITE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)

        # ---- Ground plane (oblique 3D perspective) ----
        ground = Polygon(
            [-6.8, -2.6, 0], [6.8, -2.6, 0], [7.4, -1.3, 0], [-6.2, -1.3, 0],
            fill_color=GREEN_E, fill_opacity=0.35, stroke_color=GREEN_D,
            stroke_width=2,
        )
        ground_line = Line([-6.8, -2.6, 0], [6.8, -2.6, 0], color=GREEN_D, stroke_width=3)

        # ---- Tree ----
        trunk = Line([4.5, -2.6, 0], [4.5, 2.2, 0], color="#8B5A2B", stroke_width=10)
        branch = Line([4.5, 2.2, 0], [2.6, 2.9, 0], color="#8B5A2B", stroke_width=6)
        foliage1 = Circle(radius=1.0, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([4.5, 3.1, 0])
        foliage2 = Circle(radius=0.7, color=GREEN_B, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([3.5, 3.4, 0])
        foliage3 = Circle(radius=0.6, color=GREEN_C, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([5.3, 3.3, 0])
        tree = VGroup(trunk, branch, foliage1, foliage2, foliage3)

        # ---- Newton stick figure (facing right) ----
        head = Circle(radius=0.28, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1.0).move_to([-4.5, -1.15, 0])
        body = Line([-4.5, -1.45, 0], [-4.5, -2.2, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=5)
        leg1 = Line([-4.5, -2.2, 0], [-4.7, -2.6, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=5)
        leg2 = Line([-4.5, -2.2, 0], [-4.3, -2.6, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=5)
        arm = Line([-4.5, -1.5, 0], [-3.95, -1.0, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=5)
        newton = VGroup(head, body, leg1, leg2, arm)

        # ---- Labels ----
        newton_label = Text("Newton", font_size=30, color=WHITE).next_to(newton, DOWN, buff=0.15)
        apple_label = Text("apple", font_size=28, color=RED).move_to([2.6, 3.4, 0])

        # ---- Apple fall path ----
        def apple_pos(t):
            x = 2.6 - 1.0 * t
            y = 2.9 - 6.5 * t + 1.0 * t * t
            return np.array([x, y, 0])

        path = ParametricFunction(apple_pos, t_range=[0, 1], color=YELLOW)

        progress = ValueTracker(0)
        apple = always_redraw(
            lambda: Dot(apple_pos(progress.get_value()), radius=0.16, color=RED, fill_opacity=1.0)
        )
        trail = TracedPath(
            lambda: apple.get_center(),
            stroke_width=4,
            stroke_color=YELLOW,
            stroke_opacity=0.8,
        )
        trail.set_dashed(True)

        # ---- Reveal ----
        self.play(FadeIn(title), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(ground), Create(ground_line), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(tree), FadeIn(newton), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(newton_label), FadeIn(apple_label), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)

        self.add(trail)
        self.play(
            progress.animate.set_value(1.0),
            rate_func=linear,
            run_time=4.0,
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

slides.title: One law for all
slides.caption: Universal gravitation: one law for the apple and the planets alike — the same pull that drops an apple holds every orbit.
slides.bridge: And with that one law, every orbit — the Moon's, the planets' — is the same falling apple.
slides.narration: Universal gravitation is the closing of the chain: one law for the apple and the planets alike. The same pull that drops an apple holds every orbit in the sky.
